page.overview:
What is Great Bear?

The Great Bear, also known as the Bear God or simply as Great Bear or Bear, was a powerful nature spirit venerated not unlike a deity as a protector and patron of warriors. She was a source of primal magic for her followers.

The Great Bear represented all aspects of the bear. Her roars were said to shake the land during windstorms.

Although largely benevolent, she was fickle and not always directly helpful to her faithful. While her followers were expected to use their powers to protect the weak and to strengthen those who would likewise serve to protect them, the Great Bear was predominantly interested in making sure her worshipers and their followers were respectful toward bears. Her favor was said to highlight natural beasts such as cave bears or dire bears, but did not extend to the likes of owlbears or fey bears. She expected her followers not to hunt bears without due humility, but she had no issue when a bear was slain in self-defense.

The Great Bear was venerated by many shamanistic traditions. They saw her as a perfect protector against those who would destroy or corrupt the world, and those shamans who sought to emulate the Great Bear as guardians were known as Great Bear shamans. It was said that the roar of the Great Bear could be heard in every word these shamans spoke, and their spirit companions could channel her ferocious power to maul foes and energize allies.
